answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. This is resilient because unearned rewards are capped and eventually burned, so an attacker cannot bank on a runaway Sybil campaign paying off. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a wander as the anchor of the cost.
